```python
# test_late_fee_calculator.py
from datetime import date

import pytest

from late_fee_calculator import LateFeeCalculator


@pytest.mark.parametrize("balance_cents", [0, -1, -10_000])
def test_zero_or_negative_balance_has_no_fee(balance_cents):
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 26))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(balance_cents, date(2025, 1, 1)) == 0


def test_future_due_date_has_no_fee():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 26))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, date(2026, 1, 27)) == 0


def test_fee_is_zero_through_ten_weekday_grace_days():
    # Jan 12 through Jan 23 inclusive provides 10 weekdays before Jan 26.
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 26))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, date(2026, 1, 12)) == 0


def test_weekends_do_not_count_toward_grace_period():
    # Jan 9 through Jan 26 spans 17 calendar days but only 11 weekdays.
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 26))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, date(2026, 1, 9)) == 500


def test_minimum_fee_applies_once_past_grace_period():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 26))

    # 11 weekday days past due => 1 billable day.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(1_000, date(2026, 1, 9)) == 500


def test_fee_is_prorated_and_rounded_to_nearest_cent():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 26))

    # 20 weekdays past due => 10 billable days.
    # 1,000,000 * (0.015 / 30) * 10 = 5,000 cents.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(1_000_000, date(2026, 1, 12)) == 5_000


def test_rounding_is_half_up():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 26))
    calculator.MIN_FEE_CENTS = 0

    # 1,000 * (0.015 / 30) * 1 = 0.5 cents, rounded half up to 1.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(1_000, date(2026, 1, 9)) == 1


def test_fee_is_capped_at_25_percent_of_balance():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 7, 1))

    # Raw fee exceeds 25% of this balance.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, date(2026, 1, 1)) == 2_500


def test_weekday_days_between_handles_equal_and_reverse_dates():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 26))

    assert calculator._weekday_days_between(date(2026, 1, 26), date(2026, 1, 26)) == 0
    assert calculator._weekday_days_between(date(2026, 1, 27), date(2026, 1, 26)) == 0
```

One rule inconsistency worth flagging: with balances below `$20`, the current implementation can return the `$5` minimum fee even though that exceeds the stated 25% hard cap, because `max(..., MIN_FEE_CENTS)` is applied after capping.
